candidates.topic: Why does metal feel colder than wood at the same temperature?
candidates.angle: Metal pulls heat out of your hand faster, so your skin reads the speed of heat loss, not the temperature.
candidates.hook: Metal isn't colder than wood. It's faster.
candidates.visual: a hand touching a metal bar and a wooden plank, with heat arrows leaving the hand

candidates.angle: Stale bread isn't dry: the starch recrystallises, which is why toasting it brings the softness back.
candidates.hook: Stale bread isn't dry. It's crystallised.
candidates.visual: a bread slice with starch crystals forming inside

candidates.topic: Why are shadows blue in the snow?
candidates.angle: Shadows are lit by the blue sky instead of the sun, so on white snow they turn visibly blue.
candidates.hook: Shadows on snow are blue, not grey.
candidates.visual: blue shadows of trees on white snow
candidates.notes: three entries only: a real file has about 50
